sourcedFrom: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms (2025)
cleanIntro: The Encore is a break-action frame built around interchangeable barrels, so the strip is barrel-off-frame rather than plug-only. Its breech plug is a conventional threaded plug turned out with a wrench — not the quarter-turn Speed Breech on the Triumph. Read the coverage warning in the first step before you use this guide: this manual is the MUZZLELOADER book, and the plug procedure it prints is the 209x50's.

steps.title: Check this manual covers your Encore before anything else
steps.action: The Encore is one frame with many barrels, and Thompson/Center splits the documentation the same way. This guide comes from the muzzleloader book. If your barrel is a rimfire, centerfire or shotgun Encore, this is the wrong book and the wrong procedure — T/C covers those in separate manuals.
steps.quote: Rimfire and Centerfire Rifle, Pistol and Shotgun Variations of the ENCORE® are Covered In Separate Manuals.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms — Cover — p.1
steps.warn: This manual does not cover rimfire, centerfire or shotgun Encore variations. Those have their own manuals, available free on request.

steps.title: Confirm the rifle is unprimed and uncharged
steps.action: Settle this before touching anything. A muzzleloader will not show you an empty chamber.
steps.caution: Never attempt to clean a charged or primed muzzleloading firearm.
steps.quote: Make sure that the gun is unprimed and uncharged.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms — Takedown of the ENCORE® Muzzleloader — p.39

steps.title: Tip the barrel open and sight the ignition fire channel
steps.action: Opening the barrel exposes the breech plug. Confirm no primer is seated, then hold the muzzle to a light and look through the ignition fire channel from the breech end. Light through it is the proof the barrel is empty.
steps.quote: Tip the barrel open and make sure that the gun is unprimed.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms — Unloading and Uncharging Continued — p.33
steps.warn: If you cannot see through the channel, the rifle is charged or the channel is obstructed. Stop and unload.

steps.title: If it is charged, take the plug out and let gravity unload it
steps.action: With the plug removed and the muzzle up, the powder falls out of the breech. The projectile is then pushed clear from the muzzle with the ramrod and its extension, or drawn with a bullet puller.
steps.quote: With the breech plug removed, point the muzzle up. Gravity should then cause the pellets or the loose powder to drop out.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms — Unloading and Uncharging Continued — p.33

steps.title: Remove the ramrod
steps.action: Draw the ramrod out of the thimbles under the barrel and set it aside.
steps.quote: Remove the ramrod from the thimble(s).
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms — Takedown of the ENCORE® Muzzleloader — p.39

steps.title: Take the forend off
steps.action: The forend screws back out counter-clockwise as seen from underneath. With them out the forend lifts off the barrel, which has to happen before the barrel can leave the frame.
steps.quote: Remove the forend screw(s). Turn these screws out counter-clockwise (as viewed from the bottom of the gun). Remove the forend from the barrel.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms — Takedown of the ENCORE® Muzzleloader — p.39

steps.title: Tap out the hinge pin and lift the barrel off the frame
steps.action: With the barrel tipped open, the hinge pin drives out in either direction and the barrel separates from the frame. This is the step that makes the Encore an Encore — the barrel is a module, and the frame is what you keep.
steps.quote: Tip the barrel open and remove the barrel hinge pin by tapping it out (in either direction). Remove the barrel from the frame.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms — Takedown of the ENCORE® Muzzleloader — p.39

steps.title: Unscrew the breech plug — and check which barrel you have first
steps.action: The wrench that came with the 209x50 barrel turns the plug counter-clockwise as viewed from the breech end. Expect resistance as the gas seal breaks. If your barrel is a PROHunter XT or an Endeavor, stop: those plugs have their own removal instructions in their own appendix of this manual, and the 209x50 procedure is not theirs.
steps.caution: Three different plug systems live in this one book. Confirm which barrel is in your hands before turning anything.
steps.quote: The breech plug of an ENCORE® 209x50 is removed from the barrel by turning it counter-clockwise (as viewed from the breech end of the barrel) using the wrench that was supplied with the gun. For the ENCORE® PROHunter™ XT and Endeavor - see the appropriate Appendix in this manual for breech plug removal instructions.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms — Thorough Cleaning — p.36

steps.title: Run the bore with the supplied jag
steps.action: Jag onto the ramrod, patch soaked in black-powder solvent, worked up and down the bore until the fouling stops coming out. Then dry patches until the bore is dry.
steps.prose: Black-powder residue is corrosive rather than merely dirty, and fouling raises pressure shot to shot — so it is an accuracy problem before it is a rust problem.
steps.quote: After removing all the fouling, follow up with a few dry patches to thoroughly dry the bore.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms — Field Cleaning — p.35

steps.title: Clean the frame assembly and the firing pin
steps.action: Soft bristle brush with bore cleaner over the frame, dry it, light oil. Then moisture-displacing oil into the firing pin from both the front and the back of the frame.
steps.quote: Clean the frame assembly with a soft bristle brush dampened with some bore cleaner. When the frame is dry, lightly oil it.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms — Field Cleaning — p.35

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel off the frame, plug out, bore and frame serviced. That is routine maintenance on the Encore muzzleloader. The extractor, the stock bolt torque and the reassembly detail are the manual's own disassembly section and are in the Deep Clean.
steps.quote: If the ENCORE® muzzleloader has become very dirty due to extensive firing, the shooter may want to disassemble the rifle further than just removing the breech plug.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms — Thorough Cleaning — p.38

deepSteps.title: Remove the extractor from the barrel lug
deepSteps.action: One screw retains the extractor in the lug. Back it out and the extractor lifts from its slot — it traps fouling under itself and is easy to leave dirty.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the screw that retains the extractor in the barrel lug. Then, remove the extractor from its slot.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms — Encore® Muzzleloader Disassembly Continued — p.40

deepSteps.title: Scrub the plug and both thread sets
deepSteps.action: Clean the plug, then get a stiff brush and solvent through the barrel's own breech threads. Dry both and anti-seize both before anything goes back together.
deepSteps.quote: Once removed, the breech plug should be scrubbed free of fouling and should then be lubricated with an anti-seize lubricant like T/C’s Super Lube, before reinstallation.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms — Thorough Cleaning — p.37

deepSteps.title: Flush the barrel with hot soapy water
deepSteps.action: Muzzle in a pan of hot soapy water, wet patch on the jag pumped from the breech end. The barrel draws the water through and carries the fouling out with it.
deepSteps.caution: Dry it completely before oiling. Water left in a black-powder bore rusts quickly.
deepSteps.quote: Pump the ramrod and patch up and down in the barrel. This will draw water into the barrel and flush out the fouling. When the barrel is clean, wipe off any excess water and allow it to dry.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms — Thorough Cleaning — p.37

deepSteps.title: Oil the firing pin from both ends of the frame
deepSteps.action: The firing pin channel runs through the frame and collects primer residue at both ends. Pressurised moisture-displacing oil, front and back.
deepSteps.quote: Use a pressurized moisture displacing oil to clean and lubricate the firing pin within the frame
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms — Thorough Cleaning — p.37

deepSteps.title: Torque the stock bolt — this one has a number
deepSteps.action: Most of this manual gives you feel rather than figures; the stock bolt is the exception, and over-tightening it compresses the stock material and cracks the grip. Use the factory bolt and washer.
deepSteps.quote: The stock bolt must be torqued to 50 inch-pounds (plus or minus 5 inch-pounds).
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms — Encore® Muzzleloader Disassembly — p.39
deepSteps.warn: Firing the Encore with a cracked stock can cause serious personal injury. If you see cracking near the stock bolt, stop using the stock and return it to Thompson/Center.

deepSteps.title: Seat the breech plug to snug
deepSteps.action: Thread the plug in clockwise with the wrench, feeling that it has started straight, and stop at snug. T/C defines snug by a hand test rather than a torque value.
deepSteps.caution: Be certain the threads are not cross-threaded before applying force.
deepSteps.quote: “Snug” is defined as being as tight as you can turn it into the barrel by using the breech plug wrench and turning it clockwise, while holding the barrel in your hand.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual ENCORE® Muzzleloader Rifle & Pistol Including The 209x50, ENCORE® PROHunter™ and ENCORE® Endeavor™ Muzzleloaders — ©2025 Thompson/Center Arms — Encore® Muzzleloader Disassembly Continued — p.40

cleaning.name: Bore
tasks: Solvent-soaked patches on the supplied jag until they come out clean
Dry patches until the bore is dry
Light lubricant on the bore once completely dry

cleaning.name: Frame
tasks: Soft bristle brush with bore cleaner over the frame assembly, then dry and lightly oil
Moisture-displacing oil into the firing pin, from the front and the back
Keep the lubricant light — heavy oil congeals in the cold and can stop the hammer striking the firing pin

cleaning.name: Barrel and breech plug
tasks: Scrub the plug free of fouling
Stiff brush and solvent through the barrel's breech threads, then dry
Anti-seize both the plug threads and the barrel threads
Clean under the extractor and in its slot in the barrel lug
Inspect the barrel threads for damage or corrosion and stop using the barrel if any is found

reassembly: Refit the extractor in the barrel lug and secure its retaining screw
Anti-seize the plug and the barrel's breech threads, then thread the plug in clockwise to snug
Offer the barrel to the frame and tap the hinge pin back in
Refit the forend and its screws
If the stock was off, torque the stock bolt to 50 inch-pounds using the factory bolt and washer
Return the ramrod to the thimbles
fncheck: With the rifle unprimed and uncharged, check the trigger, striker and safety mechanism for proper function before loading and firing, and confirm the barrel latches closed properly on the frame.
